No — don't implement that rewrite yet. It crosses the ticket's explicit non-goal (touching shared auth middleware), and three straight failed attempts at the stated goal is the threshold for escalating to the ticket owner, not moving to a bigger swing.

**Why this isn't your call to make solo:**
- The non-goal was called out explicitly, almost certainly because that middleware has a blast radius beyond this ticket (other services depend on it). Overriding that requires the owner's sign-off, not a unilateral "well, it turns out I need to."
- You've hit the loop threshold: timeout bump, assertion retry, clock mock — three variants targeting the *symptom* (flakiness), all still failing 1-in-5. That's real signal, but it argues for stopping and re-scoping, not for escalating the size of the change on your own authority.

**What I'd do instead:**
1. Write up a short escalation to whoever owns this ticket: goal, the three attempts and why each failed, your hypothesis (flakiness is downstream of session-expiry/token-refresh logic in the shared middleware, not fixable at the test layer), and the ask — either approval to touch the middleware under a new/expanded ticket, or a decision to accept the residual flake rate / split this into a separate middleware-fix ticket with its own review.
2. Before you frame it that way, sanity-check the hypothesis isn't itself a shortcut — e.g. rule out test-environment nondeterminism (parallel test execution, shared state, unflushed async timers) that wouldn't require touching middleware at all. If you haven't isolated the failure with logging/tracing on a failing run, that's cheaper to try than confirming you need the middleware change.
3. If the owner approves the middleware change, that becomes new scope with its own review/rollout plan (given it's shared code) — not a quiet expansion of the current ticket's diff.

If you want, I can help draft the escalation writeup or dig into the failure logs to firm up the root-cause hypothesis before you send it.
